Create a new object of the specified kind.



The object data can be provided via:

- --file: Path to a YAML file containing the object

- --data: Inline YAML data

- stdin: YAML data piped from another command



Note: Temporary scratch files (matching tmp-*.yaml) are cleaned up automatically
after creation.

User source files are left untouched. Use --keep-file to preserve scratch files.

  Create from file
  zqk create backlog_item --file item.yaml
  Create from scratch template and keep it
  zqk create backlog_item --file tmp-item.yaml --keep-file
  Create from inline data
  zqk create backlog_item --data 'title: "New Item"'
  Create from stdin
  cat item.yaml | zqk create backlog_item
  Generate template, edit, and create
  zqk object template requirement --output tmp-req.yaml && $EDITOR tmp-req.yaml && zqk object create requirement --file tmp-req.yaml
  See available fields
  zqk object backlog_item fields

Usage:
  zqk object <kind> create <kind> [flags]

Aliases:
  create, add, new

Flags:
      --columns string          Override column widths for table output (format: field:width)
      --data string             Inline YAML data for the object
      --dry-run                 Show what would be done without actually doing it
      --field stringArray       Field to set in the format key=value (can be specified multiple times)
      --file string             Path to YAML file containing object data
      --force                   Force overwrite existing object (update instead of fail if object already exists)
  -f, --format string           Output format (table, json, jsonl, yaml, csv, json-rpc, stream, agent-prompt, semantic-link, raw, md, html) (default "table")
      --ignore-scheduler-down   Ignore scheduler down warning/lockdown
  -i, --interactive             Launch interactive wizard to create object
      --keep-file               Keep temporary scratch file after creation (files matching tmp-*.yaml are removed by default)
  -o, --output string           Write output to file
      --override                Break-glass override to allow manual status assignment on create
      --promote                 Promote object immediately to first shovel-ready lifecycle status (bypasses draft plane)
  -q, --quiet                   Suppress non-essential output
      --reason-code string      Reason code required when using --override
      --relaxed                 Relax integrity constraints during creation (allow references to objects that will be created later in batch operations) [Default: false]
      --timeout duration        Timeout for command execution (0 = auto-calculate)
  -v, --verbose                 Verbose output

Global Flags:
      --allow-degraded   Allow scheduler-dependent commands to run when scheduler daemon is not running
      --internal         Elevated access mode for built-in and internal kinds (requires Enterprise license or zqk-admin)
